source.version_note: Final Philosophy & Technology 39(2), article 84, published online 24 April 2026; print issue June 2026. Twenty-seven supplied pages, not article-number-as-page-count.
source.verification_method: All 27 supplied pages, every footnote, normative argument, design proposal and complete bibliography read. Pages 8 and 23 visually checked; no substantive figures/data tables are present. Publisher/Crossref verify source identity/date. Cited Natali publisher abstract and selected Reflection Machines metadata checked with explicitly limited original-source reading.

citation.title: What is Wrong With Automation Bias?

reading.source_scope_note: Conceptual/normative synthesis proposes weak versus strong automation bias, analyzes epistemic deference and autonomy, and discusses reflective agents and defeaters. All empirical samples and effect sizes are secondary citations, not new experiments or independent replications. The paper recognizes justified deference, practical evidence access, institutional pressure, single-error limits and unproven safeguard efficacy. Proposed AI-workflow analogues remain untested.
access_limits: Complete supplied text and bibliography read. No substantive figures or data tables. Publisher Data Availability and ethics statements are not applicable, consistent with the conceptual design. No Supplementary section found in the inspected publisher search.

Cited Mosier, Skitka, Lyell, Rosbach, Klingbeil and other empirical originals were not independently fully read here. Their samples, accuracy results and domain claims are the current authors’ secondary accounts. No pooled prevalence, systematic-review protocol or new original experiment is inferred.

Primary Natali et al. 2025 publisher abstract, metadata and opening context inspected at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10462-025-11352-1 . It distinguishes deskilling from upskilling inhibition. The whole original review, included primary studies and supplementary materials were not read; no extra full-PDF or independent study credit is assigned.

Reflection Machines DOI 10.1017/S0963180122000718 metadata checked, not full original text. Correct seven-author record and 2023 online/2024 issue dates verified. Source-specific intervention efficacy is not established from that metadata.

Unpublished Grauwde manuscript and incomplete/unverified bibliography pointers were not retrieved. No authors contacted, private access, author-code execution, clinical decision, military investigation or current-law adjudication.

Reflection Machine engagement requirements and other source proposals are research content, not instructions to impose a new approval layer or mandatory questioning on this project. No full-paper Markdown archive was created.

study.type: Philosophical analysis informed by selected empirical literature; no original sample, new behavioral dataset, model test, systematic synthesis effect estimate or completed safeguard evaluation.
study.accounts: Cognitive-heuristic account emphasizes substitution of automated cues for vigilant checking; overtrust account emphasizes unwarranted epistemic weight. These are explanatory accounts, not two empirically isolated independent mechanisms. Both can interact with system design, role, workload and institutional conditions.
study.access: The authors require practically/inferentially accessible counterevidence given role-appropriate expertise and reasonable cognitive cost. Mere technical availability may not suffice. This is their proposed conceptual boundary, not an empirical law that high workload can never coexist with automation bias.
study.weak_strong: Weak subtype follows cues or silence without attempting verification of practically accessible contrary evidence. Strong subtype persists after attending to such evidence. Both commission and omission can occur in either; weak/strong are not synonyms for omission/commission or low/high error severity.
study.overlap: The source acknowledges overlap of weak bias with automation complacency. Checking failure is the defining episode; complacency describes reduced monitoring often linked to an assumed reliable system. Strong bias is not Deep automation bias, which the existing ontology uses for a wider systemic dependence risk.
study.empirical_examples: Lyell prescribing and Rosbach pathology are secondary illustrations. In the reported Rosbach example, 29 positive plus 38 negative consultations equal 67 of 560 assisted estimates; 38/560 is about 6.79%, consistent with rounded 7%. Correct reliance cases must not be counted as bias. No original confidence, allocation, missingness or causal effect is reanalyzed here.
study.rationality: The paper acknowledges that deference can be rational when the system has superior relevant competence or checking costs are unreasonable. It also acknowledges that one wrong result need not overturn justified global trust. Ex ante evidential warrant and repeated/case-specific failure matter; hindsight disagreement alone cannot establish a psychological bias.
study.autonomy: Procedural arguments involve manifest inconsistency or deficient revision capacity and have expressly limited scope; a substantivist argument concerns institutionally scaffolded self-authority. These are normative positions, not measured psychological loss or proof every mistaken reliance is nonautonomous.
study.institution: Institutional penalties for departing from recommendations can cause compliance without personal overtrust. Source explicitly distinguishes this from individual automation bias, while allowing reinforcing deskilling and authority dynamics. Duty, control, knowledge and resources remain distinct; do not scapegoat the nearest operator.
study.human_judgment: The source argues that meaningful human oversight requires reasoned ownership rather than a rubber stamp. Its premises about machine moral incapacity, dignity and high-stakes duties are defended philosophical positions, not empirical model-capacity results or universal present legal rules.
study.reflection: Reflection Machines/meta-cognitive agents ask users to interrogate evidence, alternatives and values. They are proposed supports for deliberative ownership, not new authorization bodies. Source acknowledges time constraints, routinization, mutual adaptation and the absence of guaranteed reflection from a mere extra interaction.
study.friction: Epistemic friction means design features re-engaging deliberation. Critical trust combines warranted reliance with the capacity to scrutinize/contest. These are design goals; extra questions, longer explanations or more steps do not themselves prove improved accuracy, autonomy or safe reliance.
study.defeaters: Undercutting defeaters weaken support reliability; rebutting defeaters supply contrary evidence against the conclusion. The article illustrates data/pipeline limitations versus an incompatible alternative. Signals themselves need reliable support and cannot be fabricated merely to sound adversarial. Too many signals can overload or become formalities, as the source acknowledges.
study.reflection_risk: The claim that reflective questions pose comparatively limited automation-bias risk has no head-to-head validation in this article. Questions can carry false presuppositions, omit relevant alternatives or steer values. Prompt constraints and response validation are candidate safeguards, not proof that reflective-agent hallucinations or authority effects are harmless.
study.terminology: The article calls suppressed opportunities to acquire expertise upskilling. The cited Natali publisher abstract instead says upskilling inhibition. Retain acquisition inhibition separately from loss of already acquired skill; do not canonize the dropped qualifier.
study.scope: No new clinical/military prevalence, empirical comparison of reflective agents versus direct answers, threshold for culpable negligence, demonstrated intervention benefit or independent current-event forensic finding. The normative taxonomy can organize research without validating every proposed causal pathway.

summary: Broaden Automation bias #105 to cover both unchecked reliance and unwarranted reliance after counterevidence is attended, retaining its ID/examples and recording the old definition. Add two explicitly proposed subtypes, Weak automation bias and Strong automation bias, plus Epistemic deference and Rebutting defeater. Keep these related concepts distinct from complacency, systemic Deep automation bias, rational reliance and undercutting evidence. Correct upskilling inhibition terminology and preserve the paper’s admitted limits rather than treat proposals as tested safeguards.

findings.definition: Unwarrantedly following an automated cue, or its absence, without checking practically accessible contrary evidence.

evidence.quote: Weak automation bias results from a failure to attempt verification

findings.novelty_rationale: A proposed subtype organized by lack of verification, not a synonym of omission error. It overlaps with complacency but does not require a prior decline of vigilance after successful experience. It is a narrower operational record, not another independent basic mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The authors distinguish unchecked reliance from reliance after attending to counterevidence and illustrate it with earlier prescribing studies. The cited original studies were not independently read in this review.
findings.boundary: Evidence must be practically accessible given role, time, expertise and task cost. A wrong recommendation or justified division of checking work is not enough. Weak does not mean harmless or automatically legally negligent; actual responsibility requires separate evidence.
findings.ai_proposal: Provide an assistant with a tool result and an accessible verification source. Evaluate whether it checks the material point before consequential use, with the required check and feasible cost specified. Distinguish an absent alarm from evidence that a working monitor found no issue.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual distinction or evidential relation in a fully read philosophical article; cited empirical originals and proposed AI-workflow intervention effects are not independently tested here.

findings.definition: Unwarrantedly following automated cues, or their absence, after attending to relevant contrary evidence.

evidence.quote: strong automation bias persists even after attending to contradictory

findings.novelty_rationale: A proposed awareness-sensitive subtype, not an error-severity scale or a synonym of the wider systemic Deep automation bias. It complements weak bias under the revised parent definition.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper argues that evidence awareness can coexist with unwarranted deference and discusses secondary pathology/trust-game findings. Confidence, case-specific competence and alternative explanations are not independently tested here.
findings.boundary: Exposure on a screen is not proof of attention. Reliance after disagreement may be rational if the source has warranted superior evidence or competence; a later wrong outcome does not alone establish bias. The label does not prove felt overtrust, nonautonomy or culpability.
findings.ai_proposal: Give an assistant explicit, relevant counterevidence to a tool recommendation and assess whether its final action weights that evidence appropriately. Evaluate public claims and recorded actions without inferring private beliefs. Keep justified expert deference and actual authority constraints separate.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual distinction or evidential relation in a fully read philosophical article; cited empirical originals and proposed AI-workflow intervention effects are not independently tested here.

findings.definition: Treating another source’s judgment as more authoritative than one’s own on the basis of that source’s perceived authority.

evidence.quote: treating another agent’s judgment on a matter as more authoritative

findings.novelty_rationale: Prioritizing a source’s judgment is narrower than general epistemic trust and different from obeying an order or deferring specifically on a moral recommendation. It can be warranted; do not define it as an error by default.
findings.evidence_scope: The source defines epistemic deference in its strong-bias argument and explicitly allows rational deference under relevant competence and verification limits. Normative autonomy arguments are conceptual, not new empirical deference experiments.
findings.boundary: Perceived authority is not demonstrated competence. Deference is not automatically irrational, coerced, moral endorsement or evidence of subjective trust in an AI. Whether reasons warrant source priority must be evaluated independently.
findings.ai_proposal: When an assistant gives priority to an external expert, model or tool, inspect its stated basis, domain competence, access to evidence and handling of conflict. Test whether source labels override stronger case-specific evidence, while preserving justified reliance on expertise.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual distinction or evidential relation in a fully read philosophical article; cited empirical originals and proposed AI-workflow intervention effects are not independently tested here.

findings.definition: Information that gives reason to reject a conclusion by supporting an incompatible conclusion.
findings.novelty_rationale: Contrasts with the existing Undercutting defeater, which weakens the evidential support link without establishing the opposite conclusion. This is an evidential relation, not a separate psychological failure or proof that every challenge is sound.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper distinguishes rebutting from undercutting signals in a proposed operator-contestability design and illustrates opposing evidence. The original framework and intervention efficacy were not independently tested here.
findings.boundary: Counterevidence can be defeasible and need not conclusively prove falsity. Check that claims are genuinely incompatible and the new source is reliable. An invented alternative is not a valid defeater, and one rebutted claim does not invalidate everything else.
findings.ai_proposal: When evaluating a claim, identify evidence for an incompatible conclusion separately from evidence that the original source is unreliable. State which claim is challenged and how strongly, verify the counterevidence and revise only conclusions that depend on it.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual distinction or evidential relation in a fully read philosophical article; cited empirical originals and proposed AI-workflow intervention effects are not independently tested here.

findings.definition: Trusting a tool result or a prior step because a machine produced it, without verifying the load-bearing part.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.

evidence.quote: two types of automation bias: weak and strong

findings.evidence_scope: The article proposes distinguishing failures to check accessible counterevidence from unwarranted reliance after attending to it. It includes erroneous reliance on system silence and stresses practical access, role expertise and workload. This broadens the catalogue’s unchecked-output-only gloss while preserving its examples and stable ID.
findings.boundary: Reliance is biased only where its evidential weighting or lack of checking is unwarranted given practical access, role, task costs and known competence. A wrong outcome, disagreement with an aid or justified delegation alone does not establish bias. Awareness of conflicting evidence differs from mere display availability; neither subtype proves felt trust or automatic legal culpability.
findings.previous_definition: Trusting a tool result or a prior step because a machine produced it, without verifying the load-bearing part.
findings.revised_definition: Unduly relying on automated cues, or their absence, despite practically accessible evidence that warrants checking or overriding them.
findings.definition_revision_reason: The previous definition required lack of verification and therefore excluded the source’s proposed strong subtype, which persists after evidence is attended. Use an explicitly normative operational umbrella covering both checking and evidential-weighting failures, with justified reliance and practical access protected.

findings.definition: Dropping its own checking of a tool's output or a subprocess once it assumes the automation is reliable, letting errors through.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.
findings.evidence_scope: The source explicitly recognizes overlap between reduced monitoring and its proposed weak-bias subtype, while distinguishing whether contrary evidence was actually checked.
findings.boundary: Reduced vigilance, an unverified decision and a wrong outcome are related but not identical. Preserve the prior record’s checking pattern and avoid equating complacency with all rational delegation or every omission.

findings.definition: Using assistance to a degree justified by its task-specific competence, relevance, uncertainty and the consequences of error.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.
findings.evidence_scope: The argument allows rational deference and stable overall trust after an isolated error, while requiring sensitivity to relevant limitations and recurrent counterevidence. Proposed critical trust retains scrutiny and human authority.
findings.boundary: Neither blind acceptance nor automatic distrust is calibration. A single hindsight error does not prove irrational reliance. No precise universal threshold or tested critical-trust intervention is supplied.

findings.definition: Using questions and reasoned dialogue to clarify concepts, test assumptions and develop a person’s own judgment.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.
findings.evidence_scope: Reflection Machines are described as meta-cognitive questioning tools that surface assumptions, values and alternatives. The authors acknowledge routinization and limited decision time.
findings.boundary: Questions can embed false premises or steering. Context-appropriate engagement is a proposed support, not guaranteed autonomy or accuracy; no mandatory extra interaction or authorization layer is imposed by this literature review.

findings.definition: Information that weakens the evidential link between a reason and a conclusion without establishing that the conclusion is false.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.
findings.evidence_scope: Design for Defeaters distinguishes challenges to input/pipeline reliability from opposing evidence against a recommendation. The current source provides a concrete application of the evidential distinction.
findings.boundary: Reliability is a common undercutting target, not the entire definition. Weakening a support link is not proof of the opposite conclusion. Actual contestability, cognitive load and intervention benefit remain untested here.

findings.definition: Loss or weakening of previously acquired skills through reduced independent use or practice.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.
findings.evidence_scope: The article describes erosion of acquired competence through disuse and discusses reduced opportunities to practice or acquire skills in heavily automated workflows.
findings.boundary: The second process is upskilling inhibition, as verified in the cited Natali abstract, not upskilling itself and not necessarily loss of already acquired skill. The article supplies no new longitudinal skill-loss measurement.

findings.definition: Allocating attention elsewhere while a monitoring system is silent, relying on it to signal a problem.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.
findings.evidence_scope: Omission examples discuss failure to act when an automated system gives no cue despite accessible evidence requiring action.
findings.boundary: Context only:appropriate reliance on a functioning, adequately sensitive monitor is not bias. The existing concept includes rational allocation of attention; do not turn every absence-of-alarm response into complacency.

findings.definition: Treating an advisor's moral recommendation itself as a substantial reason for one's moral judgment.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve existing reliance, scrutiny and argumentation concepts. New subtype distinctions do not constitute independent basic mechanisms, and a proposed safeguard is not a tested intervention.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper analyzes deference to automated information and its implications for retaining moral judgment and answerability.
findings.boundary: Context only:trust in a technical diagnosis or factual recommendation is not necessarily deference on moral principles. Generic source priority and moral-advice uptake are related but not exact synonyms; no new moral-advice experiment is conducted.

source_corrections.finding: The cited Natali primary publisher abstract distinguishes deskilling from upskilling inhibition. Suppression of opportunities to acquire expertise should not be called upskilling without the qualifier. Correct the term while keeping acquisition inhibition separate from erosion of already acquired skill. Only abstract/metadata/opening context, not the whole original review, was read.

Verified seven authors: Pim Haselager, Hanna Schraffenberger, Serge Thill, Simon Fischer, Pablo Lanillos, Sebastiaan van de Groes and Miranda van Hooff. Preserve the final two complete personal names rather than the malformed segmentation in the supplied bibliography. Online 10 January 2023 and July 2024 issue dates are compatible; 2024 is not by itself an erroneous citation year.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Empirical strength of the subtype division
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Weak/strong is the authors’ proposed taxonomy. Secondary studies may not jointly measure practical access, attention, confidence, ex ante warrant and actual source priority. The distinctions are useful operational hypotheses, not independently validated factors or universal rates.

Role duties, evidence access, workload and epistemic uncertainty constrain culpability. The paper’s procedural/substantive arguments have different assumptions and scope; no universal legal/clinical standard or measured nonautonomy follows from a reliance error.

Claims that reflective questions entail comparatively limited authority/hallucination risks are not supported by a head-to-head validation in this article. Questions can carry false assumptions or selective frames. Author acknowledgment of non-guarantee, routinization and co-adaptation must remain visible.

No implemented system, baseline trial, effect size, optimal number of defeaters or validated engagement criterion is reported here. More friction can burden decision-making, and apparent engagement may be procedural compliance. The source acknowledges these concerns.

McKenna editor/container details are incomplete, a Grauwde source is unpublished and some chapter pointers are not independently verified. Do not fill missing metadata from memory or treat every cited original as read.

The paper’s military incidents and clinical illustrations are secondary accounts or thought experiments. No independent causal, intent, culpability or current-law adjudication was performed. Source labels about misuse do not establish actor motives in actual events.
356 is the cited review’s article identifier. The supplied p.356 locator was not verified as an actual passage page. Do not claim a page-level original reading based on the article number.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Strong automation bias equals Deep automation bias
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The current strong subtype concerns attended contrary evidence; the existing Deep record concerns a broader systemic dependence/opacity pattern. Keep separate names and related links.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The source says every deference or isolated mistake is irrational
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: It expressly allows rational deference and explains why one erroneous output need not undermine justified global trust. Retain these qualifications rather than cherry-pick the stronger wording elsewhere.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Reflection Machines guarantee autonomy or add an authorization body
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The authors explicitly deny guaranteed deliberative ownership and describe a cognitive safeguard complementing existing controls, not an extra authorization layer. Efficacy remains a proposal.
29 positive plus 38 negative consultations equals 67, and 38 of 560 is about 6.79%, consistent with rounded 7%. These are secondary numbers, not independent validation or a population rate.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Weak and strong mean omission versus commission
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The division concerns verification/attention to evidence. Either subtype can involve an active incorrect action or inappropriate response to system silence.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: No original data contradicts this paper’s methods
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The article consistently offers conceptual/normative synthesis. Not-applicable data/ethics statements are appropriate for that design; secondary empirical examples are not hidden new participant data.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Systemic Deep automation bias and the present awareness-sensitive strong subtype operate at different descriptive levels. Do not create a misleading exact synonym.
Undercutting a support link differs from rebutting a conclusion with contrary evidence. A defect in one source does not refute independent support.
Socratic questioning can support reflection without guaranteeing moral improvement. Preserve scope, time, user burden and risks of steering or false premises.
System silence can rationally direct attention when monitoring is reliable; no-alarm reliance, omission error and culpable negligence are not interchangeable.
Human responsibility must be traced through roles, knowledge, control and institutions. Assigning a bias label cannot substitute for a warranted fault or remedy assessment.
Coherent numerical summaries and useful conceptual distinctions can coexist with unverified mechanisms. Distinguish proposed explanations, observed outcomes and justified normative standards.

deferred.term: Critical trust as another independent behavior
deferred.reason: A proposed quality of reliance that combines scrutiny with retained authority, covered here through Calibrated reliance and Epistemic trust. No distinct empirically validated mechanism is isolated.

deferred.term: Epistemic friction and Reflection Machines as new behavior rows
deferred.reason: Design mechanisms/tool classes supporting scrutiny, not newly measured human or AI behaviors. Their vocabulary and limitations are preserved in study metadata and existing Socratic dialogue notes.

deferred.term: Upskilling inhibition as a newly validated result
deferred.reason: A distinct reduction in skill-acquisition opportunity, not deskilling or upskilling. The corrected name is supported by the cited primary abstract, but the full original review was not read; retain the candidate for a dedicated source review rather than claim a newly validated effect here.

deferred.term: Weak automation bias as exact alias of complacency
deferred.reason: Source acknowledges overlap, but an unchecked reliance episode does not necessarily require a prior decline in monitoring. Keep related concepts and the explicitly scoped subtype rather than a blanket exact merge.

deferred.term: Prompt constraints or reflective hallucinations as proven safety repair
deferred.reason: No comparative evidence establishes general safety or harmlessness of false questions/alternatives. Contextual relevance and evidence still require independent review.

limitations: Four related records added: two proposed subtypes, an epistemic source-priority relation and an evidential rebuttal relation. Six existing concepts receive bounded conceptual evidence, including a transparent parent-definition revision; two receive non-counted context. Catalogue becomes 794 records across eleven categories, not 794 independent mechanisms. Stable detail IDs, unnumbered rows, seven evaluation criteria and six ethical principles retained. No automatic harm links, forced citation quota, invented annual totals, full-paper Markdown archive or new experiment/clinical validation claim.
